response.reasoning: 12,311 words of specification, and the cut is governed by what a consumer has to be able to do with the output. Each of the fifteen label definitions becomes its own unit carrying its cue and its exclusions, because a definition summarized is a definition nobody can apply -- 'the codebook defines fifteen labels' is not the definitions. The pairwise separations are cut by the boundary they resolve rather than by the table they sit in, since a reader arrives asking about one boundary. Measurements stay attached to the design decision they justify and keep their numbers: an alpha without its rater count and item set cannot be compared to anything. The evidence register is cut by epistemic class -- verified, measured in-house, design-only, contradicted, weak -- because that classification is the document's own organizing claim about itself and the part most easily lost. Quotes are kept within single lines of the source, since the blockquote markers in the definitions section make multi-line excerpts unreadable.

units.canonical_statement: The taxonomy has five coarse types and fifteen fine labels, each fine label mapping to exactly one coarse type. The mapping is a lookup table, not a judgment. The coarse types and the question each answers: case -- what happened, on one occasion; method -- what is done, required, forbidden, advised, or settled; concept -- what does this term mean; model -- why does this hold, what does it rest on, and how is it computed; system -- what is the thing built from, and what does it need to run. A sixth value, general, is assigned by code when no test fires.
units.context_note: The two-tier structure and the coarse vocabulary. The lookup-table property is what makes the coarse tier free of judgment.

units.canonical_statement: Status is one field carried by every type, taking the values floated, proposed, evidenced and settled. Floated is a point raised without being worked out -- to act on it you would have to invent the details yourself. Proposed is one approach, specified enough to build or test, with nothing validating it. Evidenced means something backs it and the backing is what makes it hold. Settled means indisputable, not the kind of thing the next study overturns.

response.reasoning: Coverage of the argument, the fifteen definitions, the pairwise rules, the mechanism, the fields and the evidence register is complete. What is missing is structural rather than propositional. The document carries a table of five coarse types with the question each answers, and the extraction states them in prose but never carries the question forms verbatim, which are the operative test a rater applies. The label-to-coarse mapping table has fifteen rows and the extraction carries four of them with their anchors; the other eleven rows exist only as the statement that they are marked DESIGN, so a reader cannot recover which fine label maps to which coarse type without the source. Two sections are represented by their conclusions but not their exemplars: every definition ships a document exemplar and a chat exemplar, and none of the thirty reach a unit, even though §3.1 makes them a required part of the definition. Two units also bundle several separately-usable rules.

findings.description: The fifteen-row label-to-coarse mapping table is not carried. Four rows appear with their anchor kappa; the remaining eleven exist only as the statement that they are DESIGN-marked. A reader cannot determine from the output that `distinction` maps to `concept` or that `dependency` maps to `system` -- the mapping is described as a lookup table but the lookup table itself is absent.

Each of the fifteen definitions carries two exemplars, one document-style and one conversational, and §3.1 makes them a required component of every definition. None of the thirty reach a unit. Since the specification's own evidence says definitions determine whether the classifier works, and exemplars are one of the three required parts, this is a systematic omission across every definition unit.

response.topic_label: the classifier's label definitions, their separations, and the measurements behind them
response.routing_reason: These units are the codebook proper and the evidence that shaped it: the fifteen definitions with their cues and exclusions, the pairwise separations that bound them, the collision tests that moved labels in and out of the set, and the reliability findings that govern how a definition must be written. They belong together because the separations are meaningless without the definitions they separate, and both were revised in response to the same measurements -- a consumer reading a definition needs to know which boundary it lost rater-pairs on.

response.topic_label: the classifier's contract, mechanism, fields and evaluation plan
response.routing_reason: These units describe the system rather than the taxonomy: what the API takes and returns, how the model is asked, what the secondary fields hold, how conversational input is treated, and what would have to be measured before the classifier is trusted. They cluster apart from the definitions because they are read by a different consumer -- someone building or evaluating the thing rather than someone applying a label -- and because the evaluation plan constrains all of them at once.

response.reasoning: This batch renders 35 units drawn from 11 parts of one specification, so every relationship here shares a single independence group and I have labelled the agreement dependent rather than independent except where the underlying evidence is genuinely several published studies. I have grouped by the part of the document each unit belongs to, because that is what determines whether two units are doing the same job: a definition and a pairwise separation both bound the same label but are used at different moments. Three groups are contested rather than convergent -- the retracted second collision test, the rejected generality test, and the boolean mechanism the corpus measured as worse than the alternative it replaced -- and in each the corpus contains both sides rather than the winning one. Judgments are made only on units this batch actually rendered.

assessments.canonical_claim: The classifier's measured reliability is high on its own corpora -- alpha 0.934 on generated statements and 0.894 on published documents -- and every claim in the specification is labelled by what backs it.
assessments.synthesis: The headline numbers and the evidence convention that qualifies them. The numbers are strong against the published comparisons -- argumentative zoning at 0.71 with seven categories, CoreSC at 0.50-0.57 with eleven, this taxonomy at fifteen labels -- but they are model raters measuring reproducibility of one codebook, not agreement with a human gold set. The three-way VERIFIED/MEASURED/DESIGN convention is what makes the rest of the corpus readable, because it separates claims with published backing from claims with in-house backing from claims with none. Only one unit from this part of the document appears in this comparison set, so the judgment is on that unit alone.
assessments.recommended_action: Keep the numbers with their rater count and corpus. An alpha without those is not comparable to anything, and the evidence convention must survive as a key to reading every other claim.

assessments.canonical_claim: The taxonomy is five coarse types and fifteen fine labels with a fixed mapping; four labels are anchored on categories with published agreement figures and eleven are not.
assessments.synthesis: The structure and the provenance of its reliability claims. The lookup-table property of the mapping is what keeps the coarse tier free of judgment. The anchor figures are borrowed: the kappa quoted is the anchor category's agreement in the cited scheme, not this label's, and eleven of fifteen labels have no anchor at all. A reader who takes the table as fifteen measured labels has misread it, and the specification says so at the point of the table. Only one unit from this part of the document appears in this comparison set, so the judgment is on that unit alone.
assessments.recommended_action: Keep the mapping and the anchors together, with the borrowed-figure qualification attached. Separating them would let the numbers read as measurements of these labels.

assessments.canonical_claim: Per-category reliability varies twofold within a scheme and the abstract categories are systematically worst, which forces three design rules.
assessments.synthesis: The empirical regularity that governs the whole specification, and the three rules it produces: the model coarse type is the known weak point so principle is written as a surface test; anything that cannot be written as a surface test should be expected near 0.45; and per-category agreement must be reported separately. The first rule generated a prediction that was later tested on this codebook and held, which is unusual -- most design rationale in this corpus is never checked.
assessments.recommended_action: Keep the CoreSC per-category figures with the three rules. The rules are only justified by the spread, and the prediction that was later confirmed is what makes them more than plausible reasoning.

assessments.canonical_claim: The general residual must be assigned by code and cannot be driven by self-reported confidence; abstention rules were measured and every one of them loses.
assessments.synthesis: A design rule with two independent kinds of backing. The published finding is that a named fallback given to a model is catastrophic -- 96.1 per cent agreement with Fleiss kappa -0.001 and the minority class never identified. The in-house finding is that self-reported confidence cannot replace it: argmax over scores holds at 0.930 but every threshold rule loses, down to 0.605 at threshold 90 with 86 per cent falling through. The mechanism is that raters disagree about their own uncertainty more than about the label, which generalizes into the corpus's most transferable claim: anything turning one classification decision into two costs more in the second step than it gains in the first.
assessments.recommended_action: Keep the threshold table intact and keep the generalization with it. The replacement mechanism -- cross-run disagreement -- is unmeasured and must be marked as such.

assessments.canonical_claim: Four labels were removed after the collision test, and the specification separates which removals the data justified from which were editorial.
assessments.synthesis: One removal was measured -- conclusion merging into finding, the worst-colliding pair at 11 co-occurrences. Three were editorial: study, permission and tradeoff drew zero assignments, but the specification states plainly that this was an item-set coverage gap and so the test did not show them weak. The two gaps left behind are named, one since closed and one still open, and the merge is criticized in the same breath for widening a label already behaving as a residual at 24 per cent. Only one unit from this part of the document appears in this comparison set, so the judgment is on that unit alone.
assessments.recommended_action: Keep the removals with their evidence class distinguished. Reporting all four as measured would misstate what the collision test showed.

assessments.canonical_claim: Status is a four-rung field on every type; asking for it improves type agreement rather than costing it, and it is dependent on type without collapsing into it.
assessments.synthesis: The largest design change in the corpus and the best-evidenced. The ladder reaches alpha 0.896, above the type taxonomy's 0.877 on the same items. The predicted weak boundary -- floated against proposed -- turned out to be the cleanest, at 2 rater-pairs, and the real difficulty is at the top. Asking for status raised type agreement from 0.841 to 0.877, inverting the main risk in the two-field design. Cramer's V of 0.595 puts 51 per cent of status outside what type predicts, and the residual-entropy table shows exactly where it pays: 1.84 bits on dependency, 0.00 on definition. All of it is four raters with no confidence intervals.
assessments.recommended_action: Keep the ladder definitions in usable form and keep the entropy table, which is the argument for scoping the field that v1 deliberately does not act on.

assessments.canonical_claim: The second collision test's headline gain was confounded by a changed item set, and the control shows the restructure bought approximately nothing.
assessments.synthesis: A retraction preserved alongside what it retracts. The headline read fine alpha 0.778 to 0.858 and coarse 0.866 to 0.927; holding items fixed, the taxonomy alone moved +0.009 fine and -0.075 coarse, while the item set alone moved +0.071 and +0.136. The claim that dissolving claim cost nothing was read off an item set containing few of the statements that make it costly. On the other set the cost is 37 rater-pairs between principle and observation. Two fixes shipped in response and the specification states it cannot separate their contributions.
assessments.recommended_action: Keep both the headline and the control. Deleting the retracted claim would remove the corpus's clearest demonstration of how an item-set confound reads.

assessments.canonical_claim: The third collision test held the item set fixed in both directions and measured +0.096 and +0.072 fine alpha, mostly attributable to two renames.
assessments.synthesis: The experiment designed to answer the previous control, run on both earlier item sets so the confound cannot recur. Driver at 0.623 became principle at 0.910; structure at 0.727 became architecture at 0.851. The renames remain confounded with the eleven repaired pointers, which the specification states rather than glossing. The strip test moves its target boundary from 37 to 11 rater-pairs but its aggregate effect is inside the noise floor, and it is retained on the judgment that a cross-coarse boundary matters more than an aggregate.
assessments.recommended_action: Keep the per-label figures and the confound. The retention decision for the strip test rests on a judgment, not a measurement, and should read that way.

assessments.canonical_claim: Codebook depth and surface-testable definitions dominate label count in determining agreement, though depth alone is not sufficient.
assessments.synthesis: Three published findings that together justify the length of the definitions section: depth and training moved kappa by 0.15-0.36 on identical documents while growing the label set from 3 to 7 cost only 0.07; concretely-described features reached F1 above 0.60 where interpretive ones fell below 0.30; and a 45-page codebook with a decision tree still yielded only 0.50-0.57. These are separate studies rather than one lineage restated, so the convergence is real -- though the specification's own register notes the reliability literature traces largely to one research lineage. Only one unit from this part of the document appears in this comparison set, so the judgment is on that unit alone.
assessments.recommended_action: Keep all three, including the third. Without the not-sufficient finding the first two read as a promise that a long codebook guarantees agreement.

assessments.canonical_claim: Every definition must carry a cue, at least two exclusions, and two exemplars, with boundaries factored out into a single separations table.
assessments.synthesis: The required shape, and the anti-drift reason boundaries live outside the definitions: a boundary stated twice can drift between the two entries. The exemplar domains are named as a known mismatch with where the anchor categories were measured, and the specification files that as a weakness in the evidence rather than something the exemplars repair.
assessments.recommended_action: Keep the required shape as a rule a definition can be checked against, and keep the domain-drift admission attached to it.

assessments.canonical_claim: The fifteen fine labels are defined by surface cues with explicit exclusions, plus the strip test that separates the taxonomy's hardest boundary.
assessments.synthesis: This is the codebook. Each definition is a cue plus exclusions written so a rater can check them against the sentence rather than infer intent, which is the property the reliability evidence identifies as decisive. They are complementary rather than convergent -- each defines a different label and none supports another -- and they are useless in summary: a reader who cannot apply the cue cannot classify anything. Several carry their own internal tests, notably the strip test, the breach test, the elevator test and the third-party test, and these are the operative content. Only one unit from this part of the document appears in this comparison set, so the judgment is on that unit alone.
assessments.recommended_action: Carry every definition's cue and exclusions verbatim in substance. Describing a definition is not carrying it, and this is the content most likely to be lost.

assessments.canonical_claim: Nineteen pairwise separations bound the labels against each other, several written in response to measured collisions.
assessments.synthesis: The pairwise rules are the bulk of a working codebook -- the scheme that reached kappa 0.71 shipped 75 of them. Each rule here resolves one boundary and several carry the collision count that prompted them, so a reader can tell which boundaries are known to be hard: principle against observation at 37 rater-pairs, principle against architecture at 17, principle against recommendation at 18, procedure against definition at 15. Two rules are any-label overrides rather than pairwise tests, and the put-forward rule explicitly outranks content. Which pairs were judged to collide is unmeasured, and the specification flags that as its own weakness.
assessments.recommended_action: Keep each separation as its own retrievable rule with its collision count. A reader arrives asking about one boundary, not about the table.

assessments.canonical_claim: The classifier asks one boolean per label and resolves by priority; this measured worse than single choice and is retained only for multi-label output.
assessments.synthesis: The most honest section in the corpus. The published finding is that binary framing beat multiclass by 90 per cent lower odds. The inference to fifteen binary probes was marked as untested, then tested, and it lost: 0.785 against 0.877 fine. Per-test agreement is good and the loss is entirely in resolution -- and the priority order is worse than resolving alphabetically. The mechanism is kept anyway for one property single choice cannot produce: 38 per cent of statements fire two or more tests. The prompt and output-format rules are separately evidenced with large effects: 26-36 points from wording alone, and recall standard deviation from 5.5 to 1.0 when option-ID letters are removed.
assessments.recommended_action: Keep the contradiction visible. A version of this that reports the binary-framing evidence without the in-house refutation would recommend a mechanism the corpus measured as worse.

assessments.canonical_claim: Conversational text classifies materially worse than document text, and three questions about how to handle it returned no evidence at all.
assessments.synthesis: Two published findings and an explicit report of absence. Six frontier models on classroom utterances reached 0.38-0.58 where human experts exceeded 0.90, and few-shot exemplars help model-dependently in both size and sign -- which conflicts directly with a single frozen prompt used across families, a conflict the specification names without resolving. On pronoun resolution, message splitting and context window size, three research angles returned nothing that survived verification, so the operating rules for chat are derived from an absence of evidence. Only one unit from this part of the document appears in this comparison set, so the judgment is on that unit alone.
assessments.recommended_action: Keep the absence-of-evidence statement as a finding in its own right. It is what makes the chat rules provisional rather than considered.

assessments.canonical_claim: The acceptance test is agreement with human labels, not with other models, and a kill criterion is pre-registered against the classifier's own usefulness.
assessments.synthesis: The evaluation plan and the evidence against the enterprise it evaluates. Inter-model agreement is shown twice not to indicate correctness.
